classification.difficultyReason: Construct three familiar line graphs on common axes, read the specified pairwise intersections and verify by direct substitution; the requested graphical method and pair selection are explicit.

children.label: a
children.prompt: On the same set of axes, plot the graphs of:

answer.short: The line $y=x$ passes through $(-1,-1)$, $(0,0)$ and $(2,2)$; see the common graph.
answer.worked:
For $y=x$:
$$\begin{align*}y&=-1 &&\text{when }x=-1\\y&=0 &&\text{when }x=0\\y&=2 &&\text{when }x=2\end{align*}$$
Plot $(-1,-1)$, $(0,0)$ and $(2,2)$, then draw the straight line through them on the common axes.

answer.short: The line $y=2x+1$ passes through $(-1,-1)$, $(0,1)$ and $(1,3)$; see the common graph.
answer.worked:
$$\begin{align*}y&=2(-1)+1=-1 &&\text{when }x=-1\\y&=2(0)+1=1 &&\text{when }x=0\\y&=2(1)+1=3 &&\text{when }x=1\end{align*}$$
Plot $(-1,-1)$, $(0,1)$ and $(1,3)$, then draw the straight line through them on the same axes.

answer.short: The line $x+y=4$ passes through $(0,4)$ and $(4,0)$; see the common graph.
answer.worked:
Find the intercepts:
$$\begin{align*}0+y&=4\\y&=4\\x+0&=4\\x&=4\end{align*}$$
Plot $(0,4)$ and $(4,0)$, then draw the straight line through them on the same axes. The point $(2,2)$ provides a check because $2+2=4$.

children.label: b
children.prompt: Use graphs to solve the following pairs of equations simultaneously for $x$ and $y$.

answer.worked:
The graphs meet at $(-1,-1)$, so $x=-1$ and $y=-1$.
Check both equations:
$$\begin{align*}y&=-1=x\\2x+1&=2(-1)+1\\2x+1&=-1=y\end{align*}$$

The graphs meet at $(2,2)$, so $x=2$ and $y=2$.
Check both equations:
$$\begin{align*}y&=2=x\\x+y&=2+2\\x+y&=4\end{align*}$$

The graphs meet at $(1,3)$, so $x=1$ and $y=3$.
Check both equations:
$$\begin{align*}2x+1&=2(1)+1\\2x+1&=3=y\\x+y&=1+3\\x+y&=4\end{align*}$$

spec.description: One common coordinate plane containing all three requested lines and their three pairwise intersections. A unit grid supports accurate graphical reading.
spec.mathematics: y=x, y=2x+1 and x+y=4 intersect pairwise at (-1,-1), (2,2) and (1,3).
